# Divinity is not captured in Religion.
I believe we are in need of a new set of frameworks between the unrecorded brutalities of the Human Experience, and the beauty of gratitude, and the truth of Rebirth.

Something connected the Existential to the Divine, the Mundane and the Humane.

Today was one of the most difficult days of my life. I honestly thought I would have a nervous breakdown. I will try to give these Physiolgical states proper labels, but the truth is not captured in the Category. Helplessness, Extreme stress, Uncontrollable rage, Extreme dissociation, Physical exhaustion, Escapism, Futility, Depression, Apathy, Fading in and out of consciousness. Desperation.

I started praying and realized; "I feel so much worse. To the point where I don't even wahnt to believe in God anymore." Thta's when miraculously (or my Cynical friend would say "you've just about had enough of this shit and flipped the swtich yourself"...) I was able to go outside with mother today for Groceries. I really did not want to

I try to capture the point-of-view exactly as I lived through it, so that we may examine it; but it is most likely gone from memory. This is tragic, becuase I can remember distinct events from recent times that had little to no salience, and yet this event of extreme stress is almost as if the body want's to evaporate it from consciousness.

This is precisely why it is so difficult to study the Human Condition; Amnesia and Memory

Theology is an incredible Academic Discipline, and a lifelong battle. However, based on what I have lived through and observed; what is observable and real are often what matters most to the Human being. Atleast, when viewed through the lens of Physiobiota.

The battle between the Divine and the Profane (a reference to Mircae Eliade)

We must also acknowledge that the Human being without functional Physiology, is incapable of foundations for the rest of Human life; at the very least, one should be absolutely grateful that one's body is not collapsed under the immense pressures of simply being alive.

Speaking of which, I believe we should hold a tradition to acknowledge the pressures of being Human; especially to the unmapped regions of the Human Experience.

Perhaps mapping the Phenomenolgoical won't cure one of madness or deter suffering

## The Mythic battle of the Human Man
We often do not recognize; but the Human Being is the most difficult, complex Mythology. The Greeks often portrayed the Human Condtiion through a mad blend between Tragedy and Comedy, but the true Human Experience is something closer to walking on a thin edge between nervous-breakdown and pure-bliss.

The Mythos of the Human Being is unlike all the other Mythologies; becuase it is both real and unbelievably so.
